content.text:
Ceate an SVG of an awkward family portrait of robots. Give each robot a distinct personality, and suggest their relationships through poses and composition. No text.

Deliver the result as image and/or video files, working in the current directory.
- Save the finished files in ./output/. Only what is in ./output/ is published as the result, so
  ./output/ holds those finished image/video files and nothing else.
- Formats: images as .png, .jpg, .webp, .gif or .svg; videos as .mp4 or .webm. At most 8 files,
  each under 2 MB; videos at most 10 seconds.
- Tools available on this machine: python3 3.15.0 (standard library only), node 26.11.1 (no npm packages), ffmpeg 9.0.2, ffprobe 9.0.2. Don't install packages or download anything.
- Keep the code you write to make the files in the working directory (its root, or a subdirectory
  like ./src/, but not in ./output/): it's published as the source. Delete intermediate files such
  as rendered frames when you're done.
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- Finish with a short summary of what you made.

content.thinking:
I'm creating an SVG family portrait of robots with distinct personalities and awkward poses.

I'm planning the composition and personality traits for each robot. The deliverables will be kept under 2 MB each, with source code stored in the working directory.

I'll build the SVG directly with code rather than generating a raster image. The portrait will use a stiff 19th-century formal composition, but the robots will awkwardly break from that pose language to show their distinct personalities.

The patriarch is a boxy industrial robot standing rigidly at the back with an awkward claw arm and bent antenna. The matriarch is a sleek domestic android sitting center with a tilted head and a firm shoulder touch.

The matriarch is composed yet over-optimized for warmth. The teenage robot slouches with crossed arms and half-lidded eyes, clearly embarrassed to be there. The eager child robot is small and round, leaning into the group with a raised arm mid-wave and glowing eyes, unable to hold still.

The middle child uses organic curves instead of the family's geometric style. It stands apart with a mouth the others lack, trying to belong.

A small roomba-like pet looks off-camera with a tangled cord around someone's foot.

Heads are rotated slightly out of alignment and heights break the classic pyramid.

I'm adding more specific awkwardness details. One robot holds another's antenna or shoulder joint in an unnatural grip. A flash reflection overexposes one visor to white while the others stay normal. The smiles are all wrong: one is a perfect geometric arc, one has no mouth and only LED dots, and another shows mismatched gear-teeth. Feet point in different directions. The eager child slightly overlaps someone in front.

Cords and cables will serve as a visual metaphor for tangled family ties. The studio backdrop is mottled gray-green or warm beige paper with slight wrinkles, and the lighting comes from front-left to cast hard shadows that misalign due to internal light sources. The style is hand-crafted SVG rather than corporate flat iconography.

The palette is now set. A warm studio backdrop of dusty rose and ochre will frame robots in desaturated metals like pewter, brass, and celadon. One mismatched cherry-red accent will mark the adopted unit or the eager child. The style evokes a mid-century editorial illustration with flat color blocks and ink outlines.

The SVG will use a wide portrait viewBox around 1600 by 1100 to read as a group photograph. The backdrop is a muted teal-gray studio sweep with a vignette, and the floor is warm walnut planks in slight perspective.

The back row is now defined. The patriarch, Unit-07, has a rectangular torso with rivets and a stoic face made of a narrow eye-slit and a single frown line. His claw arm drapes over the mother but pinches her antenna. He is gunmetal with brass joints.

A shorter uncle or grandfather sits center-back on a too-small stool. His face is a CRT monitor with curved scan lines and a gentle confused smile.

The uncle robot is now a 1950s appliance in cream enamel and walnut brown. He sits with one leg crossed awkwardly and his foot off the floor, looking nostalgic and slightly lost.

The family will be five robots plus a pet to keep the composition clear.

The grandparent is a bulbous 1950s robot with two dial eyes at different apertures. He has a grille mouth in a polite closed smile. His hands are folded in his lap but his fingers are interlocked wrong. He may wear a tiny knitted bow tie made of wire. He is formal and from another era.

The grandparent now sits in a human-shaped armchair that he perches on the edge of. The mother robot stands behind center, elegant and tall with smooth faceplate eyes and a careful smile. Her gentle hand rests on the grandparent's shoulder while her other arm wraps around the teenager who is leaning away. She tries to hold the family together in soft sage enamel. The father robot stands to her right, chunky and high-vis with a faded stripe. His LED smile is too wide, and his hand squishes the small child's head.

The father robot is ochre and steel. He is the only one looking directly at the camera with intense eye contact, showing enthusiasm that borders on overwhelming.

The teenage robot stands left of center, slightly apart from the group. He is lanky and segmented, wrapped in a hoodie-like cowl or a scarf of cables. His arms are crossed and his head turned fifteen degrees away, giving him a sideways side-eye look. One foot points outward, and there is a visible gap between him and the family that the mother is trying to close. He is mortified. His palette is matte black with a violet accent.

The child robot is now a round, short figure with huge eyes and one arm raised in a wave while the other clutches dad's leg. Its mouth is an open delighted rectangle, sitting with legs splayed and one foot missing its panel. It radiates pure chaos glee in butter yellow.

The pet sits at the front left as a low quadruped or disc robot, sniffing the teen's foot while its tail or antenna wags mid-blur. It is completely unbothered by the pose. A cable from the pet loops around the grandparent's chair leg.

I am now listing specific awkward relationship beats.

The father stands tallest and leans forward, partially obscuring the backdrop lamp. The grandparent's eyes are slightly misaligned and his hands are folded incorrectly, suggesting he is performing a rigid formality from another era.

The family's design language is now defined. The grandparent and mother share a manufacturer line, while the father is a bulkier, brighter model who married into the family. The child mixes the grandmother's roundness with the father's color, and the teenager rejects both with sharp angles.

The SVG will be drawn by hand using gradients, subtle noise filters for the backdrop texture, and clean shapes. The workspace will be checked first.

I will write the SVG directly rather than generating a raster image. I am checking what tools are available to preview or render the vector file, since standard libraries and Node lack SVG rendering capabilities.

The canvas is fixed at 1440 by 1080 in landscape. The background uses warm gray-beige walls with subtle texture, a dark wood floor in perspective, a soft studio light glow from the upper left, and a shadow blob beneath the group. The backdrop seam is slightly crooked to read as an awkward studio seam. The grandparent will sit center-left in a wooden chair.

The grandparent is now fixed at x=480, y=620 with a round refrigerator body in cream and chrome trim. His CRT head shows two mismatched eye glows—one squinted—and his grille smile is perfectly symmetrical. His hands are C-clamps interlocked at odd angles. One foot dangles off the floor while the other rests on a wheel. He carries a wire bow tie. The mother will stand behind and slightly right of him.

The mother robot is now sketched as a tall hourglass silhouette with a narrow waist and broad metal hip panels, evoking a 1960s dress. Her face is a smooth oval with almond optical sensors that glow warmly, and her smile is a shallow polite arc. She stands with one hand on the grandparent's shoulder and the other arm extended toward the teenager, fingers hovering just an inch away to mark the emotional distance. Her head tilts toward the family while her eyes look directly at the camera. The personality is one of anxious grace and careful glue.

The father robot is now a barrel-chested mass in faded safety orange and steel. His head is squarer with two circular eyes locked on the camera and a huge LED smile packed with too many teeth. He clings to the mother with his right hand near her neck joint, and his left hand squishes the child's head while one foot accidentally steps on the child's foot. The teenager stands far left.

The teenager is now a thin matte charcoal figure with a muted plum cable scarf. He has a long neck and hood-like cowl, arms tightly crossed, and a pigeon-toed stance with a lived-in dent on his shin. The gap between the mother's fingertips and his elbow is forty pixels. The child robot sits front center-right on the floor between the father's boots, a short sphere torso in butter yellow.

The child robot now has a double-exposure ghost arm to show motion during the exposure. Its left eye sits slightly higher than the right, and its mouth is an open rectangle of joy with tiny gear-teeth. One knee panel is popped open to reveal a spring. The pet is a low dachshund-roomba hybrid with mismatched ears.

The pet robot now looks up at the teenager instead of the camera. It wags its tail with a motion arc and chews a USB cable that is plugged into nothing, its other end dangling under the grandparent's chair. The personality is one of present-for-treats.

The studio chair is slightly turned. A light stand intrudes on the right edge, cropped by the frame. The image carries a vignette. The father robot has a blown-out specular highlight on his forehead from flash. The floor shadow is misregistered: the child's shadow is separate because it moved during the exposure.

The family's gazes form a relationship map: the grandparent looks left of the camera, the mother looks straight at it, the father looks through it, the teenager looks away, the child looks up at the father, and the pet looks at the teenager. The color palette is now fixed with warm gray-beige walls, dark wood floor, cream enamel, sage, steel, safety orange, charcoal, plum, butter, brass, and distinct eye glows for each character.

A subtle film grain and warm color grade will give the portrait a printed photograph feel rather than a digital UI. The SVG will be structured with grouped layers for the studio backdrop, shadows, each family member, and a final photo-finish layer for vignette and grain.

I am now locking in the exact z-order and x-coordinates. The backdrop and floor sit first, followed by the chair, then each figure layered from back to front: grandparent, teenager, mother, father, child, pet, and finally the cable and vignette. To handle overlapping arms cleanly, bodies will be drawn back-to-front while arms are placed in separate groups at the correct layer. The wall-floor horizon is fixed at y=640, with figures standing around y=920–980. The teenager is now placed at center x=250, feet at y=960, and head at y=340.

The remaining coordinates are now fixed. The grandparent sits at x=560, the mother at x=720, the father at x=980, the child at x=900, and the pet at x=340. A margin of roughly 80 pixels will give the composition breathing room. The drawing will use ellipses, rounded rectangles, and paths. No text or labels will appear; decorative rivets are allowed.

The deliverable will be a single polished SVG. A PNG duplicate is unnecessary, and the directory will be checked for any available rasterizer.

I will not invoke image generation tools. I am now writing the SVG directly to ensure the portrait is genuinely charming and readable at a glance.

The studio wall will use a radial gradient with a warmer center and cooler edges. A soft curved shadow line marks the paper-to-floor seam. The floor is a perspective trapezoid of planks converging to a vanishing point at (720, 480), with the horizon at y=620.

The teenager is now named Rowan. His body is a long slouched rectangle with a horizontal seam, and his head is a small tilted square. One leg is straight while the other crosses in front at the ankle.

Rowan’s face is a single visible plane with two narrow half-closed eyes and no smile. A plum hood sits behind his head, and one ear is an antenna with a headphone cup. His body is charcoal with shadow, his scarf is plum, and his eyes are cool blue. The grandparent is now named Pearl; she sits in a wooden chair with a curved back that is slightly too big, perched forward.

Pearl’s body is a wide cream oval with a horizontal chrome band and decorative round buttons. Her arms are short three-prong clamps clasped in her lap, one prong sticking up awkwardly. Her head is a large circle with a cream bezel and dark glass face; her eyes are two circles of unequal size, left wide and right squinting, not calibrated. A small brass wire bow sits at her neck. Her legs are short, one foot flat and the other a dangling caster wheel.

Pearl’s color palette is now fixed: cream body, shadow gray-beige, chrome gray, dark glass, and mismatched amber eye glows. A string of pearl-rivets will sit at her collar.

The mother robot is named Iris. She stands center with an A-line dress silhouette of vertical panels over a narrow torso in sage green enamel. Her head is a vertical oval with a cream face. Her eyes are symmetrical almond paths with warm amber glows. A subtle raised brow line reveals her concern while her mouth smiles.

Iris now has a pearl-rivet necklace that visually links her to the grandparent. Her hair is a swept metal bob of darker sage plates. She stands leaning toward the teenager while facing the camera, with her right hand hovering just short of his shoulder and her left hand resting on the grandparent's shoulder. Her mouth is a small closed arc. The next figure is the father robot named Bolt.

Bolt is a big rounded trapezoid torso with an orange chest plate, steel shoulders, and a faded reflective stripe. His head is wide and friendly but slightly too large. His eyes are large circles with dead-center pupils locked on the lens, thick lids, and a wide smile with too many even square teeth. His ears are bolt antennas. He holds his viewer's right arm down with his hand splayed across the child's head, while his left arm reaches behind the mother with an awkward thumb. His legs are short relative to his torso, he wears big boots, and one boot overlaps the child's foot.

Bolt’s chest panel is slightly ajar, suggesting he dressed in a hurry. His color palette is now fixed: orange body, dark gray shadow, cream face, and white teeth.

The child robot is named Pip. He sits with legs forward in a V, one leg kicked out. His head is a large circle with dad’s orange cheek circles and blush LEDs. His eyes are huge sparkles looking up at dad rather than the camera. He has an open mouth and one arm raised, plus a translucent ghost of a second arm in a different position from the shutter. The other arm wraps around dad’s boot.

Pip now has a crooked propeller or bow on his head, a plum cheek sticker, and an open knee hatch. His color palette blends dad’s yellow-orange with grandma’s roundness.

The pet robot is named Miso. He sits low on the floor as a dusty teal corgi with stubby legs and one lifted mid-step. His head turns upward toward the teenager. He has a big wet sensor eye and an antenna tail with a ghost wag.

Miso now holds a cable looped around grandma’s chair, and his collar carries a blank round tag. The composition will read as three generations: a round cream elder, a sage adult daughter, and a yellow round grandchild. Orange dad and charcoal teen break the pattern with square and barrel geometry. The gaze web is set: elder looks past the camera, mother watches the lens with a worried brow, father locks eyes on the lens, teen looks away, child faces dad, and pet faces the teen.

The touch web is now defined: the mother touches the grandparent but not the teenager, the father holds both the mother and child, the child clings to the father, and only the pet leans on the teenager’s ankle. This creates a poignant emotional layer.

Lighting will come from upper left with highlights on the left of each head, shadows falling lower right. A flash spec will sit on the father’s forehead, and ambient fill will keep the scene from looking gloomy. Contact shadows on the floor will be drawn as ellipses.

The SVG will include a subtle feTurbulence grain overlay at low opacity and soft gradients for texture.

The portrait will use minimal strokes for a polished painted-illustration look. No visible text or title elements will be included. A subtle cream photo border may frame the image to evoke a printed studio portrait.

The final design will be a full-bleed image rather than a framed mat. A subtle darkened edge vignette will give it a printed look. A faint double-exposure offset will be added to the child’s arm for extra awkwardness. The next step is to build the SVG and preview it on macOS.

I am checking which command-line tools are available to preview the SVG on macOS. I will try qlmanage, rsvg-convert, ImageMagick, or a Python script to generate a thumbnail. No browser tools are available.

I will use the installed Google Chrome in headless mode to preview the SVG without downloading anything. The file will stay under 2 MB by relying on a procedural feTurbulence filter instead of embedding a large noise image. I am now ready to write the complete SVG illustration.

I am mapping the SVG coordinate system. Each robot will be a group with local origin at its feet, using negative Y values for upward positioning. The teen is taller than the mother at 700 pixels to show an awkward growth spurt. The adult mother is 660 pixels tall, the dad 700 but wider, the sitting child 280 pixels, and the seated grandma 520 pixels.

The canvas is set to 1500 by 1100 pixels. The wall spans y=0 to 680, the floor from 680 to 1100, and the feet baseline sits at y=1000. Exact ground coordinates are now fixed: the teenager at (250, 1000), the grandmother chair at (580, 980), the mother at (760, 990), the father at (1050, 1000), the child at (960, 1010) in front of the father, and the pet at (390, 1040). A clip path will define the floor perspective. The SVG will be written as a single comprehensive file and refined after a screenshot preview.

The visual style is now fixed as a contemporary flat illustration with soft gradients, inspired by New Yorker covers and Malika Favre. Bold silhouettes will carry the personalities, not skeuomorphic greebles. Mechanical details like segmented joints, inset faceplates, antenna bolts, panel lines, and lens-shaped eyes will be kept minimal so each robot reads instantly as a machine.

The faces are now fully distinct. The teenager has a narrow visor and unimpressed slits. The grandmother’s face is a CRT screen with mismatched dials. The mother shows a worried brow beneath her smile. The father’s eyes are oversized round lenses with a huge grin. The child’s eyes are oversized lenses too, and his mouth is open. The pet is just one big lens. Small dark gaps between body parts will suggest assembled joints. A blinking eye and a ghost wave will add movement.

The awkwardness will come from physical strain, emotional distance, and over-posed gestures. A crooked chair and a studio paper crease behind the father’s head add photo-realistic humor. The output directory is being checked before writing the SVG.

A Python generator was considered for easier iteration, but editing a massive SVG string directly is simpler. The final deliverable will be a static SVG file written to the output directory.

The source file will be kept in ./src/ and copied to ./output/. I am now checking available tools and beginning to draft the SVG. A harmonious color script is being planned.

The color palette is now locked in. The warm gray wall and wood floor will anchor the scene. Each robot has a distinct palette: the teenager in dark charcoal with a purple scarf, the grandmother in cream with a dark screen face, the mother in sage green with a human-like smile, the father in orange-brown with a dark catchlight eye, and the child in bright yellow.

The pet’s palette is set to teal and cream. A shared brass accent will link the grandmother’s bow and the mother’s necklace as a family heirloom. The teenager and father will carry no brass; the child gets a tiny brass bolt, and the dad uses orange tape instead. Dad will stand on the child’s left foot, which peeks out from under his boot while the child smiles. The mother’s hand will sit 18 pixels away from the child, leaving visible air. The grandmother’s hands will form interlocking claws with one digit raised.

A soft radial gradient will deepen behind the heads in warm taupe, letting the cream-toned grandmother’s face pop against the light wall. The edges will stay lighter to keep the portrait feel classic.

A chrome rim and darker screen face will keep the grandmother from blending into the light background. The SVG will be built with grouped elements and gradients defined in a defs block. A procedural grain filter using fractal noise is being drafted to add subtle texture without embedding large image files.

A warm multiply layer will be added at the bottom for a soft photo treatment. Soft shadows under each figure will use Gaussian blur ellipses. The SVG will be wrapped in an HTML page with exact dimensions so Chrome headless can capture it reliably.

The viewBox is fixed at 1500 by 1120. The floor will be a seamless curved wood plane rising from y=760 to y=780, with a vertical gradient fill. The HTML wrapper will embed the SVG directly so Chrome headless can capture it reliably.

The chair is being placed at x=520–700 and y=560–980 with a curved high back. The grandmother’s body will overlap the seat. Dad’s head center is fixed at 150, his shoulders at 250, and his torso to 520. The mother’s head sits at 120 and the teenager’s at 160.

The child sits at y=640 with body center at 780 and feet at 1000. The pet is low at y=900–1040. The grandmother’s head sits at x=430 with body spanning y=520–780; her chair back peeks to y=360. The stacking order from back to front is background, chair back, teen body, grandmother, mother body, father body, then the mother’s reaching arm.

The arm reaching toward the teenager will be drawn after the teen so the hand overlaps in front of the backdrop. Dad’s hand on the child and the mother’s hand on the grandmother will follow those figures. The final stacking order is dad, kid, pet, cable, and vignette. I am now beginning to code the SVG and will iterate visually.

The lighting is now locked to a single upper-left direction. Every major shape will use a linear gradient with highlights on the upper-left and shadows on the lower-right. The composition will center on the main cluster while the gap and the dog provide a secondary story. A restrained detail palette keeps the illustration clean.

Each eye will carry a studio catchlight. Dad’s is a large blown-out rectangle. The teenager’s is dim. The child’s is starry. The grandmother’s CRT face gains a horizontal scan sheen. I am now writing the SVG.

A crooked studio stand and backdrop clamp will be cropped into the top corners to sell the staged portrait feel. The teenager’s hoodie is being reimagined as a plum cable-knit scarf made of looping ellipses, giving him a personalized mechanical look.

The child’s propeller bow is a two-blade spring tilted at an angle. The grandmother’s bow tie is a simple geometric shape in brass. The mother’s bob is made of segmented plates swept to one side. The father’s chest panel is a rotated rectangle with a dark gap. The child’s knee shows a spiral spring inside. The pet chews a dark cable stroke that curves across the floor and catches the grandmother’s caster. The child’s waving arm uses a double exposure: a solid arm at 70 degrees and a ghost arm at 110 degrees with 35% opacity.

The teenager’s mouth is an 8-pixel off-center line. The mother’s mouth is a 14-pixel gentle curve with her left brow slightly raised. Dad’s smile extends past his face width for an uncanny effect. The teenager’s crossed arms are tight and high, with shoulders shrugging to the ears. The grandmother leans forward eagerly but her pupils are misaligned: one looks at the camera, the other drifts outward. I am now beginning to code the SVG.

The floor path is now a smooth wood curve rising from y=740 to y=760, with faint plank lines drawn as soft strokes. The wall is a flat gradient rectangle with a large blurred ellipse behind it for a soft photographic glow. A subtle mottling of taupe ellipses will add texture without looking flat.

A radial vignette gradient will darken the bottom corners of the portrait. A thin inner shadow at the top will suggest a cyclorama backdrop. The illustration will remain pure SVG with no external images, keeping the file under two megabytes. The source will be written to ./src/awkward-family-portrait.svg and copied into ./output/.

Motion would dilute the awkward still-portrait concept, so the final artifact will remain a static SVG. Character silhouettes are being refined once more in orthographic front view, with perspective applied only to the floor plane.

The teenager will lean away at -4 degrees, the mother at +3 degrees, and the father at +2 degrees toward the center. The child tilts its head up by 8 degrees. The grandmother remains perfectly upright at zero degrees, which makes her stiffness feel awkward. Their ground positions are fixed at x=270, 700, and 1020 to form a cluster with the teen separated.

The empty space between the teenager and mother is being sized to about 30–50 pixels of bare backdrop, making it a deliberate character in the composition. The vertical crown line is now mapped as a broken pyramid: dad at y=90, mom at y=130, the slouched teen at y=175, grandma at y=340, the child at y=680, and the pet at y=900. This stair-step hierarchy reinforces the awkwardness by placing the youngest figure lowest while keeping the teenager isolated on the left.

The child will overlap the center front of the pyramid so its bright yellow wave becomes the portrait's visual anchor. Dad's orange and the teenager's dark form will serve as secondary anchors, while the grandmother's light mass and the mother's sage tones create the chromatic middle ground.

The pet will be a desaturated teal to keep it low-contrast and secondary. Small joint circles at the shoulders, elbows, and hips will use a darker metal tone so limbs read clearly. Each character is being limited to four stories: silhouette, face, prop or detail, and relationship gesture. The teenager’s side-eye visor and scuffed knee will anchor his slouching pose. The grandmother’s mismatched eyes and brass bow tie will mark her perched posture. The mother’s worried brow and hovering hand will frame her bob cowl.

The child’s silhouette is being drafted as a path with local coordinates. Dad will stand wide with a squashing hand and boot on the child’s foot. The pet will show a mid-step wag ghost.

I'll create a rich SVG illustration and render it with Chrome headless for visual QA.

The canvas will be 1500 by 1120 pixels. Each robot will be drawn as a detailed silhouette path rather than a simple geometric shape. A warm wood palette with browns and tans is chosen for the walls, floor, and characters.

The viewBox is set to 1600 by 1200. A curved wall seam sits at y=780. The family group is mapped across the canvas: a slouched teen on the left, a seated grandma in the center, a tall mom and dad on the right, a sitting kid, and a pet near the bottom.

The style will be a soft gradient with hard silhouette edges. This gives the robots a warm, storybook portrait feel rather than a flat, mechanical look.

I'm now drafting the HTML preview file and the Chrome headless command to render the SVG. I need to account for recent Chrome headless mode changes and potential browser chrome artifacts in the screenshot.

The HTML preview will use a dark background and fixed 1600 by 1200 pixel dimensions. I'll force the device scale factor to one to prevent extra height in the headless screenshot. After rendering, I'll verify the PNG dimensions with sips or ffprobe. The SVG content itself will be structured for easy iteration.

I'm refining the silhouette shapes so they remain readable at thumbnail size. The teen will have a flat, wide visor head that stands out from the other rounder forms. The grandma is a circle, the mom is tall and oval, the dad is a wide rounded squircle, the kid is a small circle, and the pet is a horizontal oval with a snout.

Body silhouettes are now defined. The teen is narrow and vertical. The grandma is egg-shaped. The mom has an A-line gown. The dad is a barrel with broad shoulders. The kid is circular. The pet is a long capsule.

Hand details will distinguish each character. The teen hides in crossed arms. The grandma uses three-prong claws. The mom has four elegant tapered fingers. The dad has heavy mittens with three fingers. The kid has round mittens with three nubs. The pet has no hands; it has paws.

Shadows will be simple floor ellipses rather than filtered group duplicates to avoid muddiness.

A soft Gaussian blur filter will create the floor contact shadows. A dark metal light stand with a softbox will sit on the far left edge to frame the portrait and add an awkward studio touch.

The light stand will be a thin, mostly cropped dark boom arm at the top left. A small green screen strip peeking through the paper backdrop on the far right is also being considered as an awkward photo artifact.

A small X of gaffer tape on the backdrop will serve as a subtle photo artifact.

An oval rug in dusty rose and cream will sit slightly askew. The teen and pet will stand partially off it, while the rest of the family sits on it. This creates a literal metaphor for the teen opting out of the family circle.

The rug will be a terracotta ellipse with a darker border and a lighter center. The teen’s left foot sits at x=280, well outside the rug’s edge at 380, so the separation is clear.

The mom’s reaching hand will cross over the rug toward the teen. Precise coordinates are now set for all six characters, including the pet’s head at (500, 1000) looking up at the teen.

The pet head is now at (400, 1080), raised toward the teen’s knee. Vertical spacing is being recalculated so heads do not crowd and feet stay on the floor. Dad and mom are tall silhouettes, the slouched teen is shorter, and the kid sits low. The floor begins around y=820.

The horizon is fixed at y=800. Standing heads rest against the wall, while the seated grandma and the child and pet sit entirely in the floor zone. The mom stands behind the grandma with a 240-pixel gap, her hand resting on the grandma’s right shoulder. Dad stands beside the mom, and the kid sits in front of dad.

The left-to-right head order is now fixed as Teen, Grandma, Mom, Dad, with the Kid standing in front of Dad. Dad’s left hand rests on the kid’s head, while his right arm reaches toward the kid or hangs akimbo.

Dad’s arms will be deliberately tangled. One hand rests on the kid’s head while the other reaches around behind the child to touch the mom’s shoulder, creating a long, awkward reach that looks like a physical tangle.

Dad’s unused right hand curls in a stiff half-curl. The kid hugs his leg. Mom is caught between the grandma and the teen. Dad stands too close to her, but their hands never meet. The couple remains physically separated.

The awkwardness is now subtler. The couple’s shoulders almost touch, creating a sliver of physical tension. The teen remains untouched except by the pet. Grandma’s eyes are misaligned: one looks toward her daughter, the other toward the camera. Dad looks directly at the viewer with intensity.

Mom’s body angles toward the teen while her eyes face the camera. The teen looks off-camera left, and the pet watches the teen. Grandma’s mismatched gaze is sharpened.

A shared design detail will unify the family: circular chest medallions and cream faceplates for mom and grandma. Dad and the kid share orange accents, bolt ears, and rectangular teeth. The teen remains visually isolated, with a cooler eye color and no inherited family traits.

The kid will carry a small sage neck ring to link all three generations. Fingers will be drawn as simple rounded rectangles. A subtle vignette frame will replace any border or text. The grandma’s chair is a mid-century wooden style with a curved back, and she is perched on the front edge rather than sitting in the seat.

The grandma’s chair back is visible behind her, and empty space sits between her body and the seat. She is sitting forward, so the seat appears behind her. Mom’s bob hair will be a dark sage oval with a side part, distinct from her lighter dress. Dad’s head is more rectangular with a heavy jaw. Small rivets will sit on dad’s shoulders and across grandma’s chest. The SVG is ready to be written.

The six characters now have distinct emotional roles. The teen looks away with crossed arms and headphones, rejecting the pose. Mom reaches with an anxious smile. Grandma sits small in her chair, eyes mismatched, hands locked in a formal performance. Dad grins wildly while smushing the child, his panel ajar and tie crooked. The kid waves delightedly at the wrong moment, his foot peeking out from under dad’s boot. The pet stays with the teen, its cable still snagged on grandma’s chair, showing a split loyalty.

The backdrop will use a pale blue-gray shadow to avoid flat brown tones. The chair’s floor shadow will be larger than the other figures’ shadows.

The child’s open knee will show a dark rectangular gap with a spiral path inside. The crooked brass bow replaces a propeller to echo grandma’s style, and dad’s hand squishes it. Gender stereotypes were avoided by framing the characters as mom, dad, and grandma rather than assigning specific genders.

Costumes are being stripped of gendered symbols. The elder will wear a brass collar ring instead of a bow tie, and the sage parent’s bob-like cowl becomes a sensor cowl with a brass heirloom necklace. Poses alone will define the relationships.

The parent’s A-line silhouette is kept as a bell-shaped chassis, distinct from dad’s barrel. The orange parent will use a peeling hazard stripe sash instead of a tie, suggesting something tried to look fancy but is coming undone. The child’s crooked brass ring matches the elder’s style yet looks like a broken family tradition. The teen keeps the headphones and avoids any formal collar.

The family portrait is now defined by machine lineage rather than gender. The sage parent is the elder’s descendant, sharing brass rings and a rounder face language. The orange parent is a different product line joined by hazard colors. The child mixes spherical form with hazard yellow and brass rings.

Face technology is being used as a form of genealogy. The elder will have a CRT dial face with no mouth. The sage parent keeps a minimal nose ridge and mouth, choosing a humanoid faceplate to seem approachable. The orange parent shows an LED display smile. The child has an open mechanical jaw. The teen almost lacks a mouth entirely.

The orange parent’s hand will be a three-finger industrial gripper slightly too large for the child’s head. The sage parent’s hand will use five articulated fingers, hovering above with an extra digit that reads as uncanny. The elder will have two folded clamp grippers. The child will use mitten paddles. The teen will keep hands buried, showing only a thumb. The pet will have paw nubs.

A small cheek dent and a sticker-free scratch will be added to the teen. The horizontal positions are being checked for balance: the sage parent and elder overlap heavily, while the orange parent and child also overlap. The gap between the teen and the elder’s arm is filled by the hand, leaving only the backdrop visible. Vertical space above the teen and elder is open, but the orange parent’s tall figure leaves less room above him.

The orange parent’s head will sit at y=80 to avoid cropping and create a slightly imposing top-heavy presence. A vignette will darken the edges and tighten the group. The backdrop behind the heads will use a soft radial gradient from cream to sage to dark brown so the faces pop. A warm floor tone will ground the composition.

The SVG will be written directly rather than generated by Python. A short animated loop was considered but rejected to keep the piece from looking cheap; only a still image is needed. The file will stay under 2 MB.

The hovering hand will use oversized, clearly drawn fingertips so the uncanny gesture reads at a glance. Only the child and the pet tail will carry motion blur; the elder and orange parent remain perfectly still to sharpen the contrast.

The elder’s half-closed eye was dropped to avoid overloading the face. The mismatched pupils now show one eye aimed at the sage parent and one at the camera, encoding their relationship. The sage parent will have a worried brow with a forced smile. The orange parent will stare with an oversized grin. The teen will look sideways. The child will look upward.

The elder’s mismatched pupils will point at the camera and the sage parent, showing a split mind between instruction and habit.

The child’s pupils will sit high and slightly right, aimed at the orange parent. The pet’s pupil will point left toward the teen. The teen’s pupils will rest far left. The orange parent’s pupils will stay exactly centered. The sage parent’s head will tilt five degrees counterclockwise toward the teen while her eyes remain fixed on the camera, creating a split between body language and the forced smile.

The orange parent will stand square to the camera, his shoulders and grin rigid, while the sage parent turns toward the teen. The elder also faces forward but his eyes fail to follow instructions. The teen tilts away and the child looks upward. Only two figures tried to face the camera directly, yet their results differ.

The orange parent will have square, wide shoulders. The sage parent’s raised shoulder toward the teen will read as a hopeful shrug. The teen’s shoulders will be high and protective. The SVG will be written cleanly. The sage arm will be drawn in front of the elder so it appears to pass above the chair.

The arm will be drawn in front of the chair to avoid clipping the oval top. If it still looks like a collision, the arm or chair will be adjusted during editing. All coordinates are being recalculated from the transform origins so the SVG numbers match exactly.

The transform origins are now fixed at floor contact. The sage parent sits at (640, 1000), the orange parent at (990, 1008), and the teen at (270, 1002). Their absolute head heights are 136, 88, and 272 pixels. Their shoulder positions are mapped in local coordinates so the SVG numbers align exactly.

The elder’s arm clears the chair by about fifty-five pixels. The child is now placed at (930, 1048) with a head radius of fifty-eight.

The orange parent’s arm will reach down and inward toward the child’s head, crossing the front of his body. The elbow will stick out left so the hand can sit on top of the kid without clipping the wave.

The orange parent’s elbow at x=800 would collide with the sage parent at x=740. Both the child’s wave and the orange arm need that same gap. The wave will be lowered and shifted toward the center-bottom so the arm can pass through without overlap.

The orange parent’s arm will stay close to his body, dropping from his left shoulder down the torso rather than crossing the gap. The child’s wave will occupy that same gap on the left side.

The child’s wave arm will extend left into the gap between the sage parent and the orange parent, keeping its hand at roughly x=800. The pet is placed at (300, 1055), small and raised toward the teen’s leg. The teen’s feet sit at x=270, so the pet can either stand near the right foot or sit in the left margin.

The pet is now placed at x=400, y=1040, sitting in the floor gap between the teen and the family. It looks back at the teen while the hand hovers above. The gap becomes a vertical column of failed connection: empty backdrop above, the hovering hand in the middle, and the pet looking up below. This creates a tender, broken narrative in the space.

The pet is now centered at 340 so its body sits flush against the rug edge. The cable will curve from the child’s hand to the elder’s chair leg. The spatial plan is complete and the SVG is ready to be written.

Comments will be added to each SVG group for easy editing. The elder’s hands will sit in his lap, visible in front of the body. His foot reaches the floor while his wheel dangles above the chair seat.

The orange parent’s chest will show a peeling hazard stripe with curling adhesive ends and a cracked panel. The sage parent’s dress will gain four vertical skirt lines and a subtle chin seam.

The SVG will be written to ./src/awkward-family-portrait.svg. Grain and vignette effects will be added last at low intensity so they can be removed if they muddy the image. No title element will be included to respect the no-text rule. The finished file will be copied to ./output/ only after QA confirms it is clean.

The elder’s chair will be a Victorian balloon style with S-curved back posts, an oval hoop, and wooden cabriole legs. A dusty rose cushion will wrap around the elder’s body like a crescent, echoing the rug and tying the chair to the floor. The elder will sit forward so the cushion remains behind them.

The elder’s cushion will sit behind them with a twenty-pixel gap on each side and above the shoulders, leaving rose visible around the body. Only the rug and cushion are textile; the robots are purely metal, so the environment becomes the sole fabric element.

Presentation attributes will be used instead of a style block for better compatibility. The ghost arm will use fill and stroke opacity. A white flash reflection and a studio floor scuff mark were both skipped to keep the image clean. The sage parent’s mouth will be a restrained curve in #b76b66 with a stroke-only outline. Her brows will be #6a5d55. The orange parent’s mouth will be a wide rounded rectangle filled dark, with six tooth rectangles and a gap between the second and third.

The child’s mouth will be an open ellipse with one big tooth and a darker pink-metal tongue. The teen’s face will show only a ten-pixel line. The elder’s mouth will form an ambiguous ventilation smile made of three horizontal slots, with the middle one slightly longer. Two small tick marks will frame the elder’s left eye as a round lens ring, while the right eye gets an offset elliptical bezel.

Overflow will be set to visible and geometric precision enabled for crisp rendering. The screenshot device scale is set to 1, with a higher value reserved for later detail checks. The finished PNG can be read back to verify the output.

A simple first draft was considered to check composition quickly, but a detailed initial pass is preferred to avoid extra rounds. The sage parent’s hand will be enlarged so the family’s near-contact feels more explicit. A ground line contact will also be added.

The sage parent’s arms will be solid sage enamel to match her body, with segmented cream joint rings on the fingers. Her faceplate will remain cream. The elder’s hands will be cream metal claws, distinct from the family palette. The orange parent’s hands will be industrial steel gray grippers.

The orange parent’s arms will be steel, matching his torso and the child’s yellow head for clear contrast. His friendly orange shell is a utilitarian panel that reveals the bare metal underneath when ajar.

The sage parent is pure enamel from head to toe, designed as a companion. The teen is matte all over, stripped of enamel or never painted. The elder keeps his original cream enamel, now yellowed with age. The child has a yellow shell with steel joints. The pet is painted teal but chipped to expose metal at one ear.

A soft shadow will sit beneath each head to ground the faces. The vignette will use a dark warm brown-black at low opacity for subtle depth. The SVG will be written now and reviewed, with two to four iterations planned.

The composition is being checked against generic robot tropes. Bold gestures and strong silhouettes should keep the portrait recognizable: crossed arms, an isolated reaching hand, a wide grin, an arm raised above the head, a large chair oval, and a low pet figure. A silhouette test will confirm each figure remains distinct even in black.

Silhouettes will be deliberately distorted for clarity. The teen will be extremely narrow, the orange parent extremely wide, the elder round, the sage flared, the child’s arm vertical and high, and the pet horizontal and low. The orange parent’s shoulders will span 300 pixels from x=840 to 1140, leaving a 100-pixel gap before the sage parent at x=740. The sage parent’s hem will extend from x=520 to 780.

The sage parent’s hem will extend behind the elder and peek out on both sides. The teen’s head top is 272 pixels, which places it below the sage parent’s chin at 264 pixels.

The teen’s head center at y=242 sits almost exactly at the sage parent’s head center, confirming their heads are level. The teen is only about 84 percent as tall as the sage parent, which is reasonable for a slouching teenager.

The teen’s head will sit at 200 pixels, near the sage parent’s eye level. This gives a tall slouching figure with a long neck and rolled-forward shoulders. The head radius is 52 pixels.

The teen’s shoulders were raised to 340 pixels, placing them only 26 pixels below the head bottom. This shrugs the neck short and keeps the slouching posture intact.

The teen’s torso is 280 pixels and legs 380, confirming the lanky slouch. His head sits at the sage parent’s cheek level, height-wise almost identical to her. The sage parent’s hand will reach toward the teen’s shoulder at (360, 360).

The reaching arm will sit at (370, 370). The gap above the elder’s head is 143 pixels. That wide empty zone may look like the arm reaches into nothing. The vertical layout needs adjustment.

The arm will sit beside the teen’s shoulder rather than floating in empty space. The gap above the elder’s head is acceptable because the chair back will fill that upper zone. The hand remains clearly next to the teen while the elder sits lower.

The composition now mirrors real family photo proportions: standing adult near the top third, seated elder in the middle, child lower. The teen’s local coordinates are fixed at head (0, -740), shoulders (-95, -680), hips (-95, -382), and feet (0, 0). The reaching hand is placed at local (-265, -635) relative to the sage parent’s translate(640, 1000), giving a short, gentle reach of 170 by 45 pixels.

The arm will be drawn as a soft, bent curve rather than a rigid line. The teen’s right shoulder is placed at x=320 and the hand at x=375, leaving a 55-pixel gap that makes the awkwardness feel realistic and painful.

I am writing a comprehensive SVG of an awkward robot family portrait.

I will hand-write the SVG for precise artistic control. The viewBox is set to 1440 by 1080. Each robot element will use absolute coordinates and grouped transforms.

I am drawing inspiration from classic awkward family portraits. The composition will feature a mottled backdrop and one robot in an awkward pose. I will avoid a white frame and instead darken the edges subtly for a full-bleed effect. A slight crooked scan rotation was considered but rejected.

The canvas itself will remain perfectly straight. The awkwardness will live entirely inside the image.

I will hand-code the characters directly into the SVG rather than generating them with a script. The overall art direction is shifting to a 1970s department-store painted portrait with dusty colors and soft airbrushed volumes.

I will try pure shapes without outlines first. If characters do not separate, I will add subtle rim lines. Each robot will have a lighter upper-left highlight edge to pop against the mid-tone background. A soft darker oval backdrop behind the group will create the mottled center effect.

The elder robot will use a dark screen face for high contrast against the lighter center. A steel rim on the cream body and the rose chair behind them will anchor the figure. The child's yellow will pop against the terracotta floor and rug.

I will add subtle contact shadows behind each head using darker ellipses offset slightly downward and rightward. I am also planning small interior details to reward closer inspection: aperture rings on the elder robot and three brass beads with brow asymmetry on the sage robot.

I am adding specific awkward details to each robot. The orange parent will show a missing tooth, peeling stripe, ajar panel, and a splayed spare hand. The teen will carry headphones, scuff marks, and a foot off the rug. The child will have a ghost arm, open knee, crushed torc, and a foot under a boot. The pet will display a chip on its ear, a cable, a ghost tail, and one lifted paw.

I will also draw the orange parent's boot overlapping the child's foot by rendering the foot first, then the boot. The drawing order is set: backdrop, floor, rug, shadows, chair, teen, sage body, elder body, then the reaching arm and hand.

The drawing order is now fully mapped. The orange parent will be drawn without its front hand and boot first. The child, including the foot under the boot, will follow. Then the orange hand will reach toward the child and the boot will overlap the foot. The pet will be drawn next. The cable will be split into two parts so it passes in front of the rug and chair leg. Chair front legs may be added if needed. A vignette and grain will finish the image. The elder robot's dangling wheel and shoe will sit in front of the chair legs.

A subtle noise filter will be added to the SVG. It uses fractal noise with a low alpha value to create a soft grain effect.

The grain overlay will use a low-opacity multiply blend instead of a color matrix. All robot eyes will share an upper-left catchlight to keep the light direction consistent.

The orange parent will receive a larger white ellipse over his head to mimic a camera flash highlight. Sage will carry a smaller sheen. The elder robot's screen face will show a horizontal reflection band.

The teen robot will be matte with only a tiny eye sheen. The child will be glossy and bright. I am refining the backdrop paper curve into a soft shadow band rather than a hard edge. I will add perspective wood plank variations using semi-transparent rectangles.

I am adding a rug stripe with an inner ellipse and a thin darker ring. I will place twenty short vertical lines along the front edge of the rug to create texture without cluttering the entire perimeter.

I decided to skip the rug fringe lines. The rug will instead use two concentric ellipses with a thin inner line, rotated slightly askew for a natural look.

The rug is being drawn as two concentric ellipses with a thin inner stroke. The teen robot sits at x=270, the pet at 350, the elder at 590, and the orange parent at 990. All positions are confirmed to stay within the rug boundaries.

The floor gradient will darken toward the bottom edge to create a foreground pool of light around the rug. I am now calculating the sage parent's body path in local coordinates, with its feet at the origin and y increasing upward.

I am drafting the sage parent's body path as a flared dress chassis with an asymmetric hem and raised left shoulder. The first complex Bezier curve was too unwieldy, so I am simplifying it to a cleaner shape.

The sage parent's body path is now fully defined as a smooth, asymmetric flared silhouette. A darker ellipse will frame the head like a nun's coif or sensor cowl, with the face cutting through it to enlarge the silhouette. The drawing order for this figure is set: cowl first, then face, then neck.

The sage parent's cowl will include a small center seam and side ear sensors. The orange parent's body path is now defined as a wide, barrel-shaped silhouette with broad shoulders and narrow hips.

The sage parent's right hem will sit at 760, leaving a 70-pixel gap between her and the orange parent's shoulder so they stand apart with the child bridging them. The orange parent's head is positioned high near the top edge for an imposing presence, though it may be lowered if it feels cropped. His shoulders will be at y=258 with a short thick neck of 32 pixels, and a cylinder will be added to complete his bulky silhouette.

The child robot will use circles for its body and head, with limbs in a deeper gold to create clear silhouette segments. The pet is being reworked into a dachshund-bot: a long body ellipse, four short legs with one lifted, a head with a snout, and a single large lens eye.

The pet's ear antenna will be one raised and one folded with a paint chip. Its tail will be a thin rod with a ghost tail at a different angle. The belly panel will be lighter, and the pet will wear a small brass collar to show it is more integrated into the family than the teen. It faces left toward the teen.

The pet will sit to the right of the teen, with its nose almost touching the teen's ankle. I am shifting the pet slightly to the right so its nose points left toward the ankle without overlapping the teen's legs.

The pet will bridge the teen and the rug. Its body extends onto the rug while its nose nearly touches the teen's foot, creating an intimate connection between the two figures.

I am dropping the pet's rug-bridge idea to keep the composition simple. The pet will stand beside the teen, off the rug, looking up at the family. Its tail will nearly reach the rug edge. The cable remains the only link to the chair.

I will write the SVG now and adjust the pet's position by screenshot rather than calculating it precisely. Facial lines will use a uniform 2.5-pixel weight with round caps and a dark brown palette. I am careful to escape XML characters.

content.thinking:
The rendered image has significant proportion and composition problems.

The teen's head is floating above the body with a short neck stub. The head group sits at -792 while the torso top is around -660, leaving a large empty gap.

The torso path does not extend high enough. The teen body is a small dark shape in the middle-left with very long thin legs reaching the floor. The overall composition resembles a lollipop.

The sage parent's head is oversized like a bobblehead. Its neck is too long and thin.

The elder robot's head is trapped inside the sage parent's torso. The elder body is a separate cream blob below with arms.

The chair is positioned behind the family. The elder robot's body and head should nearly touch in the rendered image, yet the head remains trapped inside the torso while the body sits below.

The elder's head and body are actually separate shapes. The green parent's torso overlaps the neck region, making them appear fused. The elder is drawn after the sage body, so it should sit in front, but the sage arms may be covering the neck.

The sage arms are drawn after the elder group, so they cannot be covering the neck. The green overlap between the elder head and body must come from another element.

The elder's neck path is only forty pixels long and starts near the body top. The head sits forty pixels below that point, so the neck cannot reach it. The head and body are geometrically separated.

The elder head sits at the top center of the green torso. The cream body with arms rests below at the lap level. The gap between them measures roughly eighty to one hundred pixels.

The elder head sits at y=518, which is near the image center. The body ellipse spans y=618 to 858, so the visual body is much lower than the head. This confirms the gap is real and not a drawing error.

The math shows the elder head and body should nearly touch, yet the image reveals a large gap. The dark face circle sits at roughly forty-five percent height while the cream body sits at seventy percent, confirming green space separates them. The actual rendering contradicts the intended geometry.

The elder group is drawn after the sage body, so its cream ellipse should cover the green torso. The visible gap between the head and body means the body is not rendering in front of the parent.

The math implies the elder head and body should form one continuous cream mass, not two disconnected blobs. The coordinates or image reading must be wrong.

The elder head is small and sits on the green chest. The cream body is a circle at the pelvis and does not connect to it. The teen's crossed arms are tiny bumps. I will re-read the SVG to check for missed transforms.

The orange parent is the most readable figure. Its arm reads as a hand on the child's head, and its smile is clear. The spare hand is just a blob. The peeling stripe is too weak. The orange robot's legs are hidden behind its body silhouette.

The orange robot's arm is a thin gray rectangle, and its hand is a gray blob on the yellow head. The kid is the most successful character. It waves with a subtle ghost arm, looks up, and has an open mouth. Its proportions are cute and its personality is clear. The ghost arm is too faint. The torso and knee hatch are invisible.

The pet figure is tiny and cute at the bottom left, with a cable reaching toward the chair. The teen's feet are oddly shaped ovals that sit far from the pet.

The sage parent's reaching hand clearly does not touch the teen; the arm comes from the shoulder and the gap reads well.

However, the sage parent's other hand on the elder is ambiguous. It appears as a small blob on the right side of the green body rather than resting on the elder's shoulder.

The chair is too large and the elder body does not overlap the seat, so the robot looks pasted on top rather than sitting inside. The rug placement and warm studio backdrop are effective. The orange parent's dangling arm reads as an awkward gesture. The teen's torso shape resembles a bone or pelvis instead of crossed arms.

The fixes are now concrete. Each robot needs a connected anatomy with shorter, thicker necks and heads properly attached. The elder must sit clearly in the chair with head and body fused. The teen needs a slouch with clearly crossed arms. The sage parent’s oversized head should shrink while keeping its reach gesture. The orange parent should gain visible legs and shoulder structure to stop looking like a carrot. The pet needs slight enlargement and clearer definition. The kid’s ghost arm and all hands must be made more readable.

The current style reads as generic vector blobs. I will redraw with stronger silhouettes and intentional shapes while keeping the warmth. Each robot will be built from overlapping shapes that clearly connect: head to neck, neck to torso, torso to hips, legs to hips, and arms to shoulders.

Stroke-based limbs look like noodles. I will replace them with filled tapered shapes that overlap bodies by fifteen pixels to create solid, attached joints. The new style will stay soft and warm but use clearer construction. I will estimate pixel positions from the 1440x1080 image.

The background and composition positions will stay. The teen on the left, the family cluster toward the center-right, the visible gap between the sage hand and the teen, the kid in front of the orange parent, and the pet at the teen's feet are all kept. Only the character sections themselves will be rewritten with better geometry.

The style is shifting toward a picture-book gouache look with clear overlaps and shorter necks. Head proportions are being tightened to roughly one-fifth to one-sixth of body height, down from the current one-third. Exact coordinates are being mapped on the 1440x1080 canvas: feet at y=1000, hips at y=620, shoulders at y=340, chin at y=250, and head center at y=190 with rx=58 and ry=66. The bulky adult’s head width will be about 0.45 of his shoulder span, while the sage parent’s head width will be about 0.55. Neck width will be roughly 0.35 of the head width and length about 0.25 of its height.

The bulky adult’s body will span x=520 to 780 at the hem and x=560 to 740 at the shoulders, with the head centered at (650, 190). The reaching arm is being mapped from shoulder to hand across the gap. The elder is being placed clearly in front of the sage parent at chair center x=560, with the body centered at (560, 720) and the head at (560, 520).

The elder must sit lower and more to the left. This keeps the sage parent’s right side and head visible while the elder does not block the reaching arm.

The elder head is fixed at x=500, y=560. The sage body starts near x=680, and the elder sits left of the sage center with a slight overlap. The sage’s left shoulder at x=600, y=360 sits above the elder’s head top at y=480, so the arm and shoulder remain visible in the gap. The original plan was sound; the disconnected look came from proportions rather than placement.

The sage body is a narrow dress that traps the elder head in its middle because they share the same x coordinate. The layout is being restructured with sharper offsets: the teen at x=240, the elder and chair at x=470, the sage parent at x=730 standing behind and to the right of the chair, the orange robot at x=1080, the kid at x=980 in front, and the pet at x=300.

The chair seat is fixed at y=780 and the back rises to y=420. The elder sits with hips at y=760, torso up to y=560, and head center at y=470 with a 70-pixel radius. The sage parent’s reaching arm will be routed at y=340 so it clears the chair top at y=400 and the elder head top at y=430. The teen’s legs will also be drawn as solid shapes rather than thin strokes.

The teen will be drawn as one solid charcoal silhouette: a tall, narrow torso with crossed arms, plus a head overlapping the neckline. The orange parent will become a single filled trapezoid body with thick legs visible below it, and its head will overlap the top of the body through a short neck collar rather than a long neck.

The orange parent’s head will overlap its body by thirty pixels. Its arm reaching the kid will be a thick tapered shape rather than a stroke, and its other arm will be drawn akimbo with clearly splayed fingers. The kid’s ghost arm will use forty percent opacity and larger eyes looking upward. The pet will grow to about one hundred sixty pixels and sit at the teen’s ankle as a small robot dog. Hands must be drawn as distinct fingers so gestures read clearly. The sage parent’s worried brow did not come through in the render; the face needs adjustment to show concern.

The sage parent’s face will be tightened with a smaller head and larger features so the expression reads. The elder’s mismatched eyes will be corrected so one looks sideways. The teen’s side-eye and headphones will be kept but attached to the body.

The first render reads as a generic corporate illustration. I will rewrite the SVG with stronger silhouette variety and clearer depth so each figure’s position in the composition is obvious. Mechanical details like panel lines and joint discs at the shoulders and elbows will be added to give the robots a distinct robotic identity without looking noisy. Circles placed at each joint will also cover the seams where limbs meet bodies, fixing the earlier connection problems.

The joint-disc geometry is now fixed: a sixteen-pixel circle at the shoulder, a fourteen-pixel circle at the elbow and wrist, with each limb capsule overlapping its joint. A unified light source will keep the family portrait cohesive. Coordinates are being recalculated on paper before the SVG is rewritten.

Absolute coordinates will be used throughout to avoid mis-addition errors. The teen’s left foot is at (200, 1005) and the right at (270, 998), with legs drawn as thirty-six and thirty-four pixel-wide tapered shapes. Hips sit at (248, 640) inside an ellipse of radius forty-eight by twenty-eight. The torso spans (210, 390) to (290, 660) and leans slightly left, with crossed arms drawn as two thick capsules.

The teen’s crossed arms are now mapped as two thick capsules: one from left shoulder to right waist, the other from right shoulder to left waist. The neck is twenty-two pixels wide and the head overlaps it with a forty-eight by forty-four ellipse centered at (230, 310). The sage parent’s feet are fixed at (700, 1000) and (780, 996), his hips at (740, 700), and his dress flares from shoulders at (640, 340) to hem at (860, 990). The elder’s hand is being placed at (690, 700) on the right shoulder, just inside the body’s right edge at x=680, so it does not brush the face. The sage’s dress will be drawn after this hand to keep it visible. A coordinate summary table is being prepared before writing the SVG.

The arm will pass through empty space above the elder’s head, leaving a clear gap of about one hundred pixels between the gesture and the elder. This separation makes the reach feel deliberate and unfinished rather than resting on the elder. The elder sits below this gesture, not part of it, so the arm reads as a reaching hand that passes over the elder toward the one who is pulling away.

The arm length is about 240 pixels, slightly longer than the figure’s torso but acceptable for a stylized reach. The artist will shorten it if the gesture looks like a rubber arm.

The arm will curve downward with an elbow at (510, 400), seventeen pixels below the straight line between the two figures. The shoulder-to-shoulder gap is 315 pixels, about twenty-two percent of the canvas width, which keeps the distance visible without feeling like a canyon.

The orange parent will have small hex bolt ears on the sides of its head. A soft white flash highlight at 35% opacity will sit on the orange head to suggest a power source. The elder has no antenna, the teen has headphones, and the pet has ears. The artist is now ready to write the SVG.

The orange parent’s face is being drawn with a wide mouth and six evenly spaced teeth. Its eyes are large and wide beneath a thick dark brow to create an intense stare. The kid’s pupils sit at the top of the eye whites, confirming the upward gaze.

The kid’s head is rotated slightly clockwise so its chin lifts toward the orange parent. The overlap between the kid’s head and the orange torso is intentional; it adds depth to the composition.

The orange parent’s chest panel is placed on its right side so the kid cannot obscure it. The kid’s wave reaches y=540, which sits below the stripe at y=420, keeping both visible. The sage’s dress right edge is set to x=850 so the wave fills the 140-pixel gap between the sage and the orange parent.

The 140-pixel gap between the sage and orange parents is intentional. The child sits only in front of the orange parent, so the parents remain visually separated. The sage’s arm reaches toward the teen rather than toward the orange parent, which reinforces the awkward family dynamic.

The empty space between the parents is intentional. The child and rug visually bridge them, while the teen sits outside the group. This reinforces the awkward family dynamic.

The gap between the sage and orange parents is tightened to 120 pixels. The child’s body bridges this space at the bottom, though a small gap remains on the child’s left side.

The child is centered at x=980, leaving a 40-pixel gap on each side. The wave rises from the child’s left shoulder up to (930, 500), placing the hand inside the gap between the parents. A faint ghost arm at (860, 580) with 35% opacity will overlap the sage’s outline slightly, adding an ethereal layer.

The ghost arm is being repositioned to x=880 so it sits just right of the sage’s dress and does not overlap it. The solid arm is placed at x=970, just left of the orange parent, keeping both hands inside the gap between the parents.

The orange parent’s left arm is fixed at x≥1020, keeping it clear of the wave in the gap. The child’s right foot extends to (1120, 1020), and the orange boot at (1160, 1010) will cover it; the toes must be drawn before the boot so they remain visible.

The child is drawn before the orange group so its toes remain visible beneath the boots. The orange boots will be large, rounded, and dark. The SVG will be written now with clarity as the priority; anything messy will be simplified after rendering. The floor and wall from the first version will stay largely unchanged, along with the seamless paper curve.

Dark outlines will be drawn beneath colored strokes for the limbs. The sage face group is rotated -8 degrees at (730, 200). A translucent white ellipse will sit on the elder screen to suggest a glass reflection. The elder face design from version one is kept because it reads well.

The sage face is being enlarged with stronger brows and larger features to replace the generic look from version one. The orange face structure is kept but its tooth gap is widened. The teen face is preserved and now attached to the group. The kid face is also enlarged with pupils positioned higher. The artist confirmed that the original gestures—reaching hand, wave, and smile—read clearly.

The dark teen’s alienation and the pet’s cable were already readable despite poor anatomy, so the composition concept holds. The teen will be redrawn as a single solid rounded torso rather than a collection of disconnected limbs. Its head will overlap the neck by twenty pixels to create a unified body mass.

content.text: The first pass had the right relationships, but the bodies fell apart into thin parts. I’m rebuilding the figures so the poses stay clear and everyone is actually connected.

content.thinking:
The image looks much better. I am now analyzing it carefully to identify any remaining issues.

The teen robot looks solid. The crossed arms, headphones, and side-eye clearly express its personality. The cable scarf is slightly messy but readable. Its legs are too thin and long with an awkward hip bulge. The gap to the sage hand is excellent and the foot off the rug is well placed. The silver joint on the shoulder target reads clearly.

The sage parent's reach is the strongest element. The worried brow and raised smile are subtle but readable. Its hand sits low on the elder, appearing to grasp the arm rather than the shoulder, though it remains a caring gesture. The downward arm is long and noodle-like yet still readable. The head and cowl look more proportional. The dress is plain as a green sack, but panel lines help. The right arm reaches toward the elder's hand area.

The elder robot's clasped hands accidentally form letter shapes, which violates the no-text rule. The head is too small for the round body and the arms are too simple. The mismatched eyes and vent mouth read well. The chair is thin and the cushion is barely visible. One wheel and one foot appear beneath the body.

The orange parent's face reads well with its huge smile, missing tooth, and stare. Its body is still somewhat carrot-shaped but improved by the shoulder caps. The hand on the child's head is clear. The spare hand on the right looks awkward as splayed fingers. The peeling stripe resembles a small hook and needs clearer definition. The ajar panel is readable. The arm to the child's head is tube-like but the hand shape works better. The legs are visible.

The kid robot is very effective. Its wave, ghost arm echo, and open mouth read clearly. The foot under the boot is visible. The knee hatch and torc may be too small or hidden. The proportions are the most charming.

The pet robot reads as a small dog beside the teen. Its cable to the chair looks small and may extend below the canvas edge.

The pet's eye, ears, and chip are clear. The composition reads as a family portrait with the rug separating the teen. The elder's hands must be reworked into clasped claws rather than letter shapes.

The thin chair post resembles a walking stick, making the elder look like they are standing with a cane. The seat and cushion need clearer definition so the elder reads as actually sitting.

The elder's round body sits in front of the sage parent's dress, with feet on the floor and a thin stick beside it. The seat is not obvious, so the elder looks like a small standing robot rather than someone sitting. The orange body still feels monolithic. The pet cable exiting at the bottom edge looks messy. The gap between the sage hand and the elder should stay clear. The sage parent's worried brow could be made more obvious.

The chair needs to be wider with back posts rising on both sides of the elder's head. A rose cushion halo should sit behind the seat. The elder's body must rest at the seat level with legs hanging down, rather than extending low as a large round form.

I am now drafting the replacement for the elder's hands. The letter-shaped claw lines will become solid rounded mitten clamps or overlapping circles with short vertical fingers, so the gesture reads as clasped hands rather than text.

The elder's hands are now drawn as solid mitten clamps with short vertical fingers, so they no longer read as letters. The pet's cable will stay on the floor as a simple curve looping above the bottom edge without dropping below y=1070.

The pet cable path is now a smooth curve looping around the front chair leg. The teen's legs will be thickened to stroke 48 and integrated into the torso so they no longer look like thin sticks.

The teen's legs will gain knee and ankle circles to look mechanical rather than like sticks. The sage arm is long because it reaches from the shoulder to the elder's mid-body; raising the elder higher or placing the hand on the shoulder would shorten it.

The orange parent will gain a waist break and hip joints to stop looking like one long carrot. The peeling stripe will be enlarged into a more obvious curl. The kid's ghost arm and boot toes will be made clearer.

The visible toes in front of the black boot will be enlarged. The pet robot will be slightly larger so it reads clearly. The chair seat is now fixed at y=880, wider than the elder body and sitting just below the body bottom at y=860. The back posts will extend from y=480 beside the head down to the floor, with a curved top rail peeking above the shoulders on both sides. A rose cushion will sit behind the head and shoulders.

The elder body spans x=474 to 698. The left chair post at x=450 sits clearly beside the head, but the right post at x=730 is hidden behind the sage parent's dress. This makes the chair look like a single left-side cane rather than a proper two-post seat.

The chair will be drawn in front of the sage parent so both posts remain visible. The elder will sit on top of the chair, covering its center mass and framing the head between the two posts.

The sage parent's dress was covering the chair, which is why the posts disappeared. The drawing order is now fixed: background, sage legs and dress, chair, teen, elder, sage arms, then the remaining figures. The downward arm will sit in front of the elder.

The elder's hands are being redrawn as solid mitten clamps. The seat will be made more obvious. The pet cable is being simplified to avoid looking like a letter or dropping off the canvas. The teen's chest cable will be replaced with two clean loops instead of a tangled scribble. The sage parent's left brow will be raised more dramatically so the worry reads at a glance.

The sage parent's smile will be tightened and narrowed to contrast with the raised left brow. The orange hand on the child's head is clear. The kid's ghost arm opacity may be raised to 0.45. The teen's side eye and headphones are readable.

The elder's "AY" hands will be removed so the dials read as clocks and circles. The pet cable path is being checked to ensure it stays inside the frame.

The pet cable curve dips below the canvas edge at y=1100, so it will be clipped above y=1065. The plug rectangle is also being redrawn. The orange parent's body will gain a waist seam and hip bolts to break up its monolithic shape. The sage dress still looks too plain with only three faint vertical lines.

The vent mouth, dials, and orange teeth are confirmed to read as mechanical shapes rather than letters. The chair seat will be a solid horizontal ellipse in contrasting wood, extending beyond the elder on both sides so the body sits clearly above it with a small gap revealing the front edge.

The elder body will overlap the seat slightly so it reads as sitting. The legs will hang from under the body. The back posts will sit at x=430 and x=740, rising from y=500 to the floor. The curved top rail between them will peak at y=470 behind the head.

The curved top rail is being raised to y=430 so it sits just above the elder's crown as a thin wooden halo. The reaching arm at x=586 is calculated to pass near y=355, keeping it clear of the rail.

The reaching arm will now end at the elder's right shoulder instead of dropping to mid-body. The rail and arm are confirmed clear of each other. I am preparing a large coordinate rewrite for the elder group.

The elder body is too large and low. It currently covers the seat entirely and extends below it, so the figure looks like a standing robot with legs hanging out the bottom rather than someone sitting. The chair will be moved to after the sage-body so it sits in front of the dress.

The elder body is being placed at y=730 so its bottom sits at 840, exactly on the seat top at 846. The head will rest at y=520 and connect to the body via a neck from 580 to 640. The left chair post at x=430 is being checked for overlap with the teen.

The right chair post will sit just outside the elder body, visible over the sage dress. Armrests are being skipped to avoid clutter. A rose cushion behind the elder will frame the shoulders.
Reviewing the chair, elder hands, teen legs, and sage face sections to prepare precise replacements.

content.thinking:
Several targeted fixes are planned.

The chair will be placed between the sage and the elder to avoid overlap with the teen. The elder's sitting position and hand placement also need correction.

The teen's legs will be thicker with visible knees. The sage hand will be retargeted to the elder's shoulder at (700, 640). The elder will sit on a wide chair seat at y=860, with legs drawn emerging from beneath the body before the torso.

The chair will be a separate group placed between the sage and the elder. The elder's legs will draw first, then the body covers them. Feet will sit on top of the seat and appear in front.

The chair SVG is being drafted with wood-colored back posts, a curved rose back panel, a wide dark wood seat ellipse, and front legs extending to the floor.

The back posts will sit outside the elder's body so they remain visible on both sides. The rose panel and top rail will show above and beside the head, completing the chair illusion. The elder body ellipse is centered at (586, 730) with a radius of 100 by 108, placing its bottom edge at 838 to rest directly on the seat.

The seat ellipse extends to y=896, so the front of the wood seat will remain visible beneath the elder's body. The sides also spill past the narrower body edges, creating a visible brim that reinforces the perched-on-seat illusion.

The elder's legs will extend from (530, 820) to (520, 960) on the left and (650, 820) to (655, 1000) on the right. The caster wheel sits at y=970 and the shoe at y=1005. Both start just under the body at y=820.

The hands will be solid clasps around (580, 800) in front of the torso. The arms will curve shorter and thicker from the shoulders to the lap. Fingers will be drawn as overlapping rounded shapes so they do not look like letters.

The sage hand will be placed at (698, 640) on the elder's right shoulder. The arm curve is being adjusted to end at (710, 630) so the hand sits cleanly on the shoulder.

The teen's legs will use thicker strokes and knee circles. The sage's brows are being made more asymmetric with a higher left eyebrow and a smaller smile. A cable path is being added from the sage to the elder.

The cable path now wraps around the chair front leg, ending in a loop near (470, 1020). The pet is being enlarged slightly for better readability.

A waist line will be added to the orange robot to break the carrot shape. Hip bolts may be added as well. The elder's arms are being shortened so they no longer look like letter curves. The dial hand pointing up is fine. The sage dress will cover the chair if it sits after her.

The drawing order is finalized. The sage body and dress will be drawn first, followed by the chair, then the teen, then the elder, and finally the sage arms. This ensures the chair sits between the sage and the teen, so the teen remains visible in front of any overlap.

The teen's torso will extend lower to swallow the hip ellipse, removing the separate bulge. The leg paths will start from inside this extended torso.

The ghost arm opacity will be raised from 0.38 to 0.48 for a clearer double exposure. The orange robot's hand is acceptable as-is. The elder's right arm may extend past the chair post, but that is fine since the elder sits after the chair.

The chair seat is drawn before the elder, so it should be covered by the body. The visible front edge is intentional. The legs extend below the body as described.

The headphone cable is in world space while the headphone rotates with the head, so they may not connect cleanly. It should be reworked to start at the earcup and drop straight down the chest in two loops that stay on the torso rather than crossing the face.

The second parent is also grinning too hard at the camera, with a spasming hand and a panel open. The child is waving and looking at the parent, with toes under a boot.
